web_events.answer: This week's US economic data releases include the May Consumer Price Index (CPI) which showed headline prices rising 4.2% year over year and 0.5% on the month, marking a three-year high. The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) is expected to leave interest rates unchanged at 3.50%-3.75% during their meeting on June 16-17. Additionally, May retail sales data is due on Wednesday, providing insight into consumer behavior amid rising prices.

web_events.answer: China's May economic data reveals a weakening consumer market with retail sales falling 0.6% from the previous year, marking the first decline in over three years.
